steps.text: Bring water to a boil in a large pot over high heat. Add salt, sugar, and dill sprigs; stir until sugar has dissolved. Pour in shrimp and cook until the shells turn pink, and the meat is no longer translucent, 3 to 4 minutes. Strain the shrimp through a colander, discard dill sprigs, and chill until cold in the refrigerator, about 30 minutes.

Once shrimp have cooled, peel and devein them; discard the shells. Whisk together oil, vinegar, minced dill, salt, and pepper; toss with shrimp meat to coat. Cover, and chill overnight in the refrigerator; serve with sprigs of fresh dill.

raw_recipe.headline: Dilled Shrimp (Rejer)
raw_recipe.description: You can't have a Danish holiday meal without endless platters of dilled shrimp. Served on a red serving platter, it makes the perfect Christmas dish that will have your guests heaping up pyramids of shrimp on their plates. No Scandinavian buffet would be complete without it!

review.reviewBody: Served this as an appetizer last night for a dinner party and everyone raved about it! Fabulous, and very easy. I love any dish I can make ahead and just take out of the fridge to serve. I used uncooked but peeled, deveined shrimp with tails on which made it even easier as I didn't have to peel the shrimp. I cut the salt in half and will probably use even less next time I make this. Also squeezed a bit of fresh lemon over the shrimp before serving. Thanks for this recipe - I'll definitely make it often!
This is a great way to serve shrimp. Cooked exactly as stated but used dried dill instead of a fresh sprig. I also don't think the sugar is necessary. Yum!
Very nice but felt it needed more marinade especially dill.

Just made this for a family Christmas gathering and everyone LOVED it! I used Key West Pink fresh frozen shrimp that I thawed and deveined prior to cooking but left the shells on to better retain the flavor. Cooled then shelled and added to the marinade,to which I added more fresh dill than the recipe called for, probably about 1/2 cup minced and no, it wasn't too much. Very good, will be doing this many more times!

Fussy husband approved. Since he does (insists) on doing the majority of the cooking, this rating speaks volumes! I typically use white balsamic vinegar which to me takes most everything up a notch :)

I thought it tastes very simple and delicious. I didn't change anything of the recipe. The only thing I still don't understand is how to devein shrimp after it is cooked. I couldn't pick the vein up like a string any more, so I cut into the back with a sharp knife and when I found black vein, I scraped it out with the tip of the knife. I will check other people's reviews in search for other answers to my question.

I made this dish (exactly as written) for New Years as a change of pace from the usual shrimp ring. My husband and daughters ate it all and my oldest said it is one of her favorite dishes that I've prepared, which is why I'm giving it 5 stars. Thanks for the great recipe!
Great recipe! Have made it many times over the last couple of years.
